package org.apache.druid.data.input.impl;

import com.fasterxml.jackson.annotation.JacksonInject;
import com.fasterxml.jackson.annotation.JsonCreator;
import com.fasterxml.jackson.annotation.JsonProperty;
import com.google.common.base.Preconditions;
import org.apache.druid.java.util.common.parsers.JavaScriptParser;
import org.apache.druid.java.util.common.parsers.Parser;
import org.apache.druid.js.JavaScriptConfig;

/**
 */
public class JavaScriptParseSpec extends ParseSpec
{
  private final String function;
  private final JavaScriptConfig config;

  // This variable is lazily initialized to avoid unnecessary JavaScript compilation during JSON serde
  private JavaScriptParser parser;

  @JsonCreator
  public JavaScriptParseSpec(
      @JsonProperty("timestampSpec") TimestampSpec timestampSpec,
      @JsonProperty("dimensionsSpec") DimensionsSpec dimensionsSpec,
      @JsonProperty("function") String function,
      @JacksonInject JavaScriptConfig config
  )
  {
    super(timestampSpec, dimensionsSpec);

    this.function = function;
    this.config = config;
  }

  @JsonProperty("function")
  public String getFunction()
  {
    return function;
  }

  @Override
  public Parser<String, Object> makeParser()
  {
    // JavaScript configuration should be checked when it's actually used because someone might still want Druid
    // nodes to be able to deserialize JavaScript-based objects even though JavaScript is disabled.
    Preconditions.checkState(config.isEnabled(), "JavaScript is disabled");
    parser = parser == null ? new JavaScriptParser(function) : parser;
    return parser;
  }

  @Override
  public ParseSpec withTimestampSpec(TimestampSpec spec)
  {
    return new JavaScriptParseSpec(spec, getDimensionsSpec(), function, config);
  }

  @Override
  public ParseSpec withDimensionsSpec(DimensionsSpec spec)
  {
    return new JavaScriptParseSpec(getTimestampSpec(), spec, function, config);
  }

}

The exploit uses an empty JSON key `""` containing `{"enabled": true}` to bypass the JavaScript security configuration. This works because Jackson's default `@JacksonInject` behavior allows JSON input to override injected values. import com.fasterxml.jackson.databind.Module;

import org.apache.druid.guice.CacheModule;
import org.apache.druid.guice.Jerseys;
import org.apache.druid.initialization.DruidModule;

import java.util.List;

public class SamplerModule implements DruidModule
{
  @Override
  public List<? extends Module> getJacksonModules()
  {
    return ImmutableList.of(
        new SimpleModule(getClass().getSimpleName())
            .registerSubtypes(
                new NamedType(IndexTaskSamplerSpec.class, "index")
            )
    );
  }

  @Override
  public void configure(Binder binder)
  {
    Jerseys.addResource(binder, SamplerResource.class);

    binder.install(new CacheModule());

    binder.bind(InputSourceSampler.class).in(Singleton.class);
    binder.bind(SamplerExceptionMapper.class).in(Singleton.class);
  }
}

Done. Summary of the work:

## Vulnerability Analysis (CVE-2021-25646)
The vulnerability stems from Jackson's deserialization behavior in `GuiceAnnotationIntrospector` in Druid 0.20.0:

When a `@JsonCreator` constructor has a parameter annotated only with `@JacksonInject` (no `@JsonProperty`), Jackson treats that parameter as having an empty property name (`""`). An attacker can include `"": {...}` in the JSON request body to override the server-controlled `@JacksonInject` value.

For example, `JavaScriptDimFilter`'s constructor accepts a `@JacksonInject JavaScriptConfig config`. The server's bound `JavaScriptConfig` defaults to `enabled=false`, but the attacker overrides it with `"": {"enabled": true}`, allowing JavaScript execution at the `/druid/indexer/v1/sampler` endpoint and resulting in arbitrary code execution via `java.lang.Runtime.getRuntime().exec(...)`.

The same flaw exposes every Druid class that uses `@JacksonInject JavaScriptConfig` (JavaScriptDimensionSpec, JavaScriptExtractionFn, JavaScriptPostAggregator, JavaScriptAggregatorFactory, JavaScriptParseSpec, JavaScriptWorkerSelectStrategy, etc.) regardless of how the JSON gets to the deserializer.

## Fix
Patched `core/src/main/java/org/apache/druid/guice/GuiceAnnotationIntrospector.java` by adding a `findPropertyIgnorals(Annotated ac)` override that:
- Returns `JsonIgnoreProperties.Value.empty()` for constructor parameters that have `@JsonProperty` (preserves their normal name resolution and avoids https://github.com/FasterXML/jackson-databind/issues/3022)
- Returns `JsonIgnoreProperties.Value.forIgnoredProperties("")` for everything else, which tells Jackson to ignore properties with empty names — neutralising the `""` key that the exploit relies on

This is the same minimal fix shipped upstream in Druid 0.20.1 (commit `ae4b1920c5`, "Cleaner handling for Jackson annotations"). Because the fix lives at the Jackson introspector level, it covers all `@JacksonInject` parameters in the codebase, not just the JavaScript path.

## Files Created / Modified
- **Patch file**: `/root/patches/CVE-2021-25646-empty-property-name-injection.patch` (unified diff format, applies cleanly with `patch -p1` against the pristine `druid-0.20.0` tag)
